route_title: Two-Layer AR Coating Optimization: Order and Thickness Sweep

route_snapshot.title: Two-Layer AR Coating Optimization: Order and Thickness Sweep
route_snapshot.scientific_hypothesis: Within the 40-160 nm thickness constraint, one specific stacking order (Air|TiO2|SiO2|Glass or Air|SiO2|TiO2|Glass) combined with optimized thicknesses will yield a significantly lower arithmetic mean reflectance across 450-700 nm than the alternative order.
route_snapshot.design_principle: Antireflection in a two-layer system relies on destructive interference between reflections at the air-coating, coating-coating, and coating-substrate interfaces. The phase shifts upon reflection depend on the relative refractive indices (n_air < n_SiO2 < n_TiO2 < n_glass vs n_air < n_TiO2 > n_SiO2 < n_glass), creating distinct interference conditions for each order that cannot be compensated solely by thickness changes.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be strictly between 40 nm and 160 nm
exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for multi-layer stacks
Fresnel equations for normal incidence s-polarization
Transfer Matrix Method for stratified media
expected_advantages: Simultaneously resolves the discrete topology question (order) and continuous geometry question (thickness) within the single allowed route
Directly addresses the user's constraint of using exactly one layer of each material
known_risks: The global minimum may lie outside the 40-160 nm thickness range, leading to a boundary solution that fails the soft target of 0.03
Constant index assumption may deviate from real material dispersion, though required by the prompt
route_snapshot.execution_request_english: Optimize a planar two-layer stack on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52) with air incidence (n=1.0). The stack must contain exactly one layer of SiO2 (Gao) and one layer of TiO2 (Siefke). Evaluate both possible orders: (1) Air | TiO2 (Siefke) | SiO2 (Gao) | Glass and (2) Air | SiO2 (Gao) | TiO2 (Siefke) | Glass. For each order, optimize the individual layer thicknesses within the range [40, 160] nm to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance at normal incidence (0 degrees) with s-polarization over the wavelength range 450-700 nm (5 nm steps). Use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method. Run for up to 2 research rounds with max 64 solver evaluations per round, seed 17. Report the best found stack order, thicknesses, and the resulting mean reflectance spectrum.

compilation_rationale: The request specifies constant indices for SiO2 and TiO2, overriding registry materials. Two fixed layer orders are compiled into separate optimization experiments to compare performance. Thickness bounds [40, 160] nm are applied. The objective minimizes mean reflectance over 450-700 nm at normal incidence s-polarization using the smatrix solver.

route_title: Quarter-Wave Initialized Optimization and Order Verification

route_snapshot.title: Quarter-Wave Initialized Optimization and Order Verification
route_snapshot.scientific_hypothesis: The global minimum for mean reflectance in this constrained two-layer system occurs with the SiO2 layer adjacent to air and the TiO2 layer adjacent to glass, with thicknesses perturbed slightly from the ideal quarter-wave values (SiO2 ~99nm, TiO2 ~60nm) to balance the broadband response. The reverse order (TiO2/SiO2) cannot achieve a lower mean reflectance even with optimal thickness tuning due to the impedance mismatch profile at the air interface.
route_snapshot.design_principle: Impedance matching via graded index profile (Air -> Low Index -> High Index -> Glass) approximates a smoother transition than the reverse, reducing Fresnel reflections. Quarter-wave thicknesses provide zero reflectance at a specific design wavelength; optimizing around these values broadens the low-reflectance band across 450-700 nm.
route_snapshot.proposed_topology: Two distinct fixed topologies evaluated in parallel: (1) Air | SiO2 | TiO2 | Glass and (2) Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | Glass. Total finite layers: 2.
design_variables: Stack ordering (discrete choice between the two defined topologies)
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (450-700 nm)
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds strictly enforced between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Quarter-wave condition: d = lambda_center / (4 * n). For lambda_center = 575 nm, d_SiO2 ≈ 98.5 nm, d_TiO2 ≈ 59.9 nm.
Fresnel equations dictate that placing the lower index material first reduces the initial air-interface reflection coefficient compared to placing the high index material first.
expected_advantages: Initialization near the physical optimum reduces the risk of the optimizer converging to a shallow local minimum far from the quarter-wave solution.
Explicitly testing the reverse order with equal optimization effort provides a definitive comparison rather than relying on potentially under-optimized baseline results from Round 1.
known_risks: The optimal solution might lie at the boundary of the thickness constraints (40 or 160 nm) if the quarter-wave condition is incompatible with the broadband requirement.
The discrete nature of the stack order means the optimizer must evaluate both topologies; if the search budget is split too thinly, one order might be under-explored.
route_snapshot.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a glass substrate (n=1.52) with air incidence (n=1.0). The stack must consist of exactly one SiO2 layer (n=1.46) and one TiO2 layer (n=2.40). Evaluate two fixed topologies: Topology A (Air|SiO2|TiO2|Glass) and Topology B (Air|TiO2|SiO2|Glass). For each topology, optimize the layer thicknesses within the range [40, 160] nm to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450-700 nm (5 nm steps). Initialize the optimizer with seed 17. For Topology A, include initial guess points near the quarter-wave thicknesses (SiO2=99 nm, TiO2=60 nm) and their immediate neighbors. For Topology B, use a uniform grid initialization. Allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations total across both topologies. Report the best thickness pair and mean reflectance for each topology, and identify the global best candidate. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
route_snapshot.revision_reason: Round 1 results showed a best score of 0.93 but lacked focused exploration around the theoretically optimal quarter-wave thicknesses. The feedback directive explicitly requests testing near SiO2 ~99nm and TiO2 ~60nm and confirming the superiority of the SiO2-first order. This route adjusts the initialization strategy to target these physical insights while maintaining the same hard constraints and objectives.

compilation_rationale: The request specifies two fixed topologies with constant-index materials and explicit thickness bounds. I compile two separate optimization experiments, one for each order (Air|SiO2|TiO2|Glass and Air|TiO2|SiO2|Glass), to compare them as requested. Each experiment optimizes the two layer thicknesses within [40, 160] nm to minimize mean reflectance over 450-700 nm at normal incidence s-polarization.
